nodes.label: Criminal Legal System and Jurisdiction
nodes.summary: Foundation of HK criminal jurisdiction, court hierarchy, and constitutional/NSL limits.

nodes.label: Territorial / Extra-Territorial Jurisdiction
nodes.summary: Hong Kong courts exercise criminal jurisdiction over offences committed within Hong Kong; extra-territorial jurisdiction only where expressly provided by statute or international law.

nodes.label: Basic Law Article 19
nodes.summary: Courts have jurisdiction except over acts of state; NPCSC may interpret.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Ma Wai Kwan David [1997] HKCFA 28
nodes.summary: Continuity of law and jurisdiction after 1997.

nodes.label: Ng Ka Ling v Director of Immigration [1999] 2 HKCFAR 4
nodes.summary: Constitutional jurisdiction; courts may review legislation for inconsistency with Basic Law but cannot strike down.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Lai Chee Ying (2021) 24 HKCFAR 121
nodes.summary: No jurisdiction to review NPC/NPCSC acts.

nodes.label: Jurisdiction Flow: Determine Locus → Check Extra-Territorial Reach → NSL Rules
nodes.summary: Step 1: Determine locus of offence. Step 2: Check if statute provides extra-territorial reach. Step 3: If national security offence, apply NSL separate jurisdictional rules.

nodes.label: Courts Exercising Criminal Jurisdiction
nodes.summary: Magistrates' Courts (Cap 227), District Court (Cap 336, max 7 years), Court of First Instance (Cap 4, judge and jury), Court of Appeal (Cap 4), Court of Final Appeal (Cap 484, leave required).

nodes.label: Magistrates Ordinance (Cap 227)
nodes.summary: Summary trial, committal, bail, transfer jurisdiction.

nodes.label: District Court Ordinance (Cap 336)
nodes.summary: Indictable offences transferred from magistrates; max sentence 7 years (or aggregate).

nodes.label: High Court Ordinance (Cap 4)
nodes.summary: Original jurisdiction over most serious indictable offences; trial by judge and jury.

nodes.label: Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal Ordinance (Cap 484)
nodes.summary: Final appellate court; leave required; only 'final decisions' in criminal matters, except where miscarriage of justice.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Chen Keen [2013] 4 HKC 615
nodes.summary: Final vs interlocutory decision in CFA jurisdiction.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Milne John (2019) 22 HKCFAR 218
nodes.summary: Prosecution appeal; bail pending CFA proceedings.

nodes.label: Constitutional Limits and NSL-Specific Procedure
nodes.summary: Acts of state (Art 19 Basic Law) non-justiciable. NPCSC interpretations binding. National Security Law (NSL): designated judges, special bail rules, restricted legal representation (overseas lawyers need CE certificate – Cap 159 s.27A).

nodes.label: Legal Practitioners Ordinance (Cap 159) s.27A
nodes.summary: Overseas lawyers need Chief Executive certificate for NSL cases.
